notes: wowsims-forever models one Hunter spell package for all three specs (engine spec mapping, design section on the APL rotation lane); Beast Mastery, Marksmanship and Survival share this same Aimed Shot / Multi-Shot weave and differ mainly in which cooldowns and secondary shots they lean on. The cited Warcraft Tavern BM guide's own numbered rotation (step 7) says to cast and refresh Serpent Sting -- it only calls Arcane Shot a leveling-only filler, not Serpent Sting -- so Serpent Sting upkeep is kept here, in the same shape as hunter-marksmanship's. Bestial Wrath is added as the spec's own cooldown, timed with Rapid Fire so both land in the one burst window a Classic-length fight allows. Every rank named here is checked against this build's own spellconst: the fork's p1.apl.json preset names Multi-Shot as spell 25294, which does not exist in this build at all (Multi-Shot only has one rank here, 2643), and calls Serpent Sting rank 8 when 25295 is actually rank 9 in this build's spellconst -- both fixed here rather than copied stale. Aimed Shot (20904) is registered by the engine again since 2026-09-28 (its registration had been commented out, and the cast line was declared inert until then). What did need fixing: nothing in this site's request pipeline (sim/request) ever sets a character's DistanceFromTarget, so every hunter starts at 0 -- under Multi-Shot, Serpent Sting and Aimed Shot's own ExtraCastCondition floor of 12 (core.MinRangedAttackDistance), which also gates the ranged auto-attack itself (sim/core/attack.go's startPull). A `move` prepull action to 30 yards is added so this and every future simulation of this spec actually has a ranged auto-attack and can cast its ranged abilities. Under this smoke build specifically (no gear equipped anywhere) the ranged weapon's SwingSpeed is the Weapon{} zero value, which collapses the ranged swing timer to its 500ms cast-time floor (sim/core/attack.go's WeaponAttack.updateSwingDuration: curSwingDuration = weapon.SwingSpeed / hasteMultiplier = 0) -- a real ranged weapon's positive SwingSpeed does not have this problem. The resulting sub-GCD auto-shot loop saturates the character's action economy so completely that the priority list, including Multi-Shot and Serpent Sting, never gets a decision window in this one bare-weapon run; this is a new engine-side artifact of the no-gear smoke build (recorded for the engine ledger), not a defect in this rotation's gates. Rotation-accuracy program diagnosis (2026-09-28), inert 2643 and 3045: both are unranked single-id abilities in spellranks.json (Multi-Shot's rank-1 id 2643 is the ONLY row spellranks.json carries for this ability in this build -- its higher client ranks 14288/14289/14290/25294 are simply absent from the data entirely -- and Rapid Fire 3045 is genuinely a single, unranked ability), each with rank:0 and a real nonzero level column (2643 at 18, 3045 at 26) that the ladder's own idLearnLevel deliberately skips for EVERY rank<=0 row (the same skip that correctly keeps Bloodrage/Judgement -- true always-known, no engine level gate at all -- from being wrongly treated as gated). Multi-Shot and Rapid Fire are the opposite case: sim/hunter/multi_shot.go's rank 1 carries RequiredLevel 18, and sim/hunter/rapid_fire.go's registerRapidFire returns immediately `if hunter.Level < 26`, so the engine really does gate both on a level spellranks.json's rank<=0 shape cannot express to this harness. Fix round: not declared inert here (that would wrongly tell the level-60 smoke test to expect them permanently unresolved, when the pinned engine resolves both fine above their real gate). Fixed instead with a small, explicit, engine-verified allowlist in sim/internal/spellranks (singleTierLevelOverrides) and its read-only ladder-side mirror (sim/request/ladder.go's idLearnLevel): only these two ids (plus druid-feral's Tiger's Fury, the same shape) are promoted from 'untracked, always learned' to a real single-tier gate, so Bloodrage (spellranks.json row: level 10, rank 0) and Judgement (level 4, rank 0) are untouched -- neither is actually level-gated by the engine at all (checked directly: sim/warrior/bloodrage.go and sim/paladin/judgement.go register unconditionally), so a blanket 'rank 0 with Level>0 means level-gated' rule would have wrongly broken them. See this lane's report for the fuller diagnosis and the data-pipeline follow-up (Multi-Shot's own higher client ranks 14288/14289/14290/25294 are simply missing from spellranks.json entirely, a separate gap from this level-10 false unresolved). 2026-10-21 (ladder rotations lane): Arcane Shot also fires while Aimed Shot cannot start (the next auto shot is within a second, which is Aimed Shot's own gate). At level 50 the ladder's 1.6 second ranged weapon never leaves a window for Aimed Shot, which then sat ready forever and held Arcane Shot behind it, so the shot never fired. 2026-10-31 (theorycraft audit fixes): Multi-Shot and Aimed Shot share one 6 second cooldown in Forever (client spell category 2; both tooltips say so), and the engine now runs them on one timer. On that shared timer the instant Multi-Shot outdamages Aimed Shot, whose 2 second cast pauses the auto shot, so Multi-Shot fires on every cooldown and Aimed Shot is only the pre-pull opener. The lines that used to read Aimed Shot's cooldown now read Multi-Shot's, the same clock. Client 1.60.1.70707 (2026-10-31): Aspect of the Hawk's ranks 1-5 fell to 15/22/30/38/47 ranged attack power, so rank 6 (14322, 55) is the strongest from level 58 and the prepull casts it; through 70685 rank 5 (90) was, and rank 6 was skipped as inferior. 2026-11-03 (sim-accuracy round 13, server hotfix push for 1.60.1.70753): Aimed Shot about doubled at every rank, Arcane Shot, Serpent Sting, Aspect of the Hawk and Trueshot Aura went up. Aimed Shot now takes the shared cooldown whenever the next auto shot is more than 1.2 seconds away, and Multi-Shot only when the cast would hold an auto shot; measured beyond error at seeds 1 and 50001. 2026-11-04 (sim-accuracy round 20): Blizzard's 3 November notes put 15% of ranged attack power on Arcane Shot and 5% a tick on Serpent Sting, so Multi-Shot is now the worst shot for its mana. Multi-Shot waits while mana is under a quarter and Arcane Shot's own mana gate is gone; measured beyond error at seeds 1 and 50001 on 180 s and on 420 s fights. 2026-11-05 (sim-accuracy round 21): Hunter's Mark goes up 20 seconds before the pull, ahead of the aspect, so the mana it costs is back by the pull. The engine used to hold the mark to 0 as if it were a damaging shot (it carried a spell damage proc mask), where it failed under Aimed Shot's cast or spent the opening global; the fork now gives it no damage mask. 2026-11-05 (sim-accuracy round 21, G1 from guide-accuracy round 20): below 34 Serpent Sting and Arcane Shot no longer wait on Multi-Shot's cooldown while Multi-Shot is held under a quarter mana (gate: not spellIsKnown Explosive Trap 13813, trained at 34). Before this, at 18 and 19 the card cast nothing but Hunter's Mark below a quarter mana, and at 20-33 only Aimed Shot spent the cooldown. Bare: Beast Mastery +5.5% (20) to +1.6% (33), Marksmanship +4.0% (20) to +0.1% (33); 34 and above unchanged (the same branch everywhere lost 0.1-0.6% at 35-49 and 60, while 50-59 would gain 2-3.5%, which no level test can scope today). 2026-11-05 (sim-accuracy round 21, auto shot): in Forever an Auto Shot fires while Aimed Shot (and Sniper Shot) is being cast (beta logs, nine hunters: about 60% of Aimed Shot casts carry an Auto Shot inside the cast). The engine now keeps the auto timer running through the cast (fork, RangedShootsWhileCasting), so the old gate (cast only right after an auto shot fires) is gone: Aimed Shot goes whenever the shared cooldown is up. 2026-11-05 (round 21, rendered-card review): the low-mana branch of the sting and Arcane Shot loses its below-34 scope. With Aimed Shot ungated the branch ties everywhere from 34 and fixes a real stall at 50-51, where the top Aimed Shot rank is out of reach under a quarter mana and the shared cooldown sat ready with nothing to spend it (Marksmanship 50: Arcane Shot 10.1 -> 19.8 casts).

sources.label: wowsims-forever default hunter priority list (shared across all three hunter specs; Multi-Shot and Serpent Sting ranks corrected against this build)
Warcraft Tavern: Classic Beast Mastery Hunter rotation (Aimed Shot on cooldown, Serpent Sting refreshed, Multi-Shot filler, Bestial Wrath and Rapid Fire together as the one burst window)
Forever Sixty default rotation, unvalidated until the nightly job runs

priorityList.notes: Hunter's Mark whenever the target is not marked. One mark per target is enough: if another hunter's mark is already up, leave it.

Bestial Wrath on the pull with Rapid Fire and your trinkets, then again every two minutes. The pet hits 50% harder for 18 seconds and shrugs off fear, so send it in first and press it once the pet is on the boss.

Rapid Fire on the pull as an auto shot leaves and the shared cooldown is about to come back, and from 40 with Bestial Wrath. The haste starts on a fresh shot and the first Aimed Shot lands inside it. It is a five minute cooldown, so a normal boss fight gets one: put your trinkets and your damage racial, if your race has one, on the same press.
Aimed Shot whenever the cooldown it shares with Multi-Shot is up. Your auto shots keep firing while you cast it, so there is no auto shot to wait for, and it hits harder than Multi-Shot.

Multi-Shot on cooldown at 18 and 19, while you are above a quarter of your mana. From 20 Aimed Shot takes the shared cooldown whenever it is up, so Multi-Shot is for packs and for moving. It is the worst damage for its mana you fire, so it is the first shot to go when the mana runs low.

Serpent Sting when it has under 1.5 seconds left, and from 18 never while the shared cooldown is about to come back, unless you are under a quarter of your mana. Refreshing any earlier throws away a tick. Every tick carries 5% of your ranged attack power on top of its own damage, so from 18 it does more for its mana than Multi-Shot: keep it rolling for the whole fight. From 18, when both are ready and your mana is above a quarter, the shared cooldown goes first: a late Multi-Shot, or from 20 a late Aimed Shot, pushes it back, while a late sting costs only a moment of its damage.

Arcane Shot to fill a gap; from 18, only with the shared cooldown over a global away or under a quarter mana. It is instant and never holds an auto shot, and every hit carries 15% of your ranged attack power, so from 18 it does more for its mana than Multi-Shot: keep it going even when the mana runs low.

panel_when.1: when Hunter's Mark is not on the target
panel_when.2: on cooldown, with Rapid Fire and trinkets
panel_when.3: as Auto Shot fires with Multi-Shot nearly ready
panel_when.6: when Serpent Sting has under 1.5 s left

7.text: when Multi-Shot is 1.5+ s from ready or mana is 25% or less
